results.title: Nigel Farage warns Britain faces RIOTS if Andy Burnham reverses Brexit
results.description: Nigel Farage has warned that Britain will face riots if Andy Burnham reverses Brexit just hours before the Prime Minister sits down with EU leaders in Brussels. The Reform UK leader fumed about the “betrayal” of the British people, calling Mr Burnham's mooted reset deal a “cynical” move to rejoin the bloc. He cautioned that such a stark reversal of Britain’s democratic will, voting to leave the EU by 52 per cent to 48 per cent in 2016, would undermine the nation’s democratic principles. “What really upsets me, makes me angry actually, is that the biggest democratic vote in history is about to be unravelled by a man with no mandate,” Mr Farage said. He was referring to Mr Burnham’s path to replacing Keir Starmer as Prime Minister: winning the Makerfield by-election and ultimately the keys to No10 with just 24,927 votes in the Manchester seat. Mr Farage argued that successive administrations had “betrayed” the result of the 2016 referendum, leaving democracy at “a very fragile point”. “What is the point of voting if governments do the opposite to what they say they're going to do again and again and again?” He warned that a growing number of young people were contemplating “direct action” as an alternative to the ballot box. His remarks come in the shadow of weeks of violent disorder across the European continent, where thousands were arrested after buildings were burned down and shops looted across France and beyond. Mr Burnham reignited the Brexit debate by floating the possibility of standing on a manifesto commitment to rejoin the EU at the next general election. In September, the Prime Minister went so far as to say “we could go all the way” to full membership. Downing Street sought to distance itself from those remarks, insisting today that Burnham has “not proposed rejoining the EU”. It's too late. He has let the genie out of the bottle… This debate is back,” Mr Farage said “I'm the only person you even trusted. I've never wavered. I have never changed my view,” he added. The Prime Minister has ruled out restoring freedom of movement during this parliamentary term but has left the door open to doing so in the future. However, Mr Burnham will discuss granting 100,000 EU visas as part of the Youth Mobility Scheme, which would permit a set number of under-30s to live and work in the UK, at tomorrow’s summit. Mr Farage slammed the proposal as “the beginning of total open door immigration”. The Reform leader also addressed his party's recent polling slump, which dropped to 19 per cent in the latest More in Common survey. It puts Reform in a distant third, behind Labour at 29 per cent and the Tories at 25 per cent. When pressed on whether he had “blown” his shot at power, Mr Farage was defiant. “No, far from it,” he declared. Our Standards: The GB News Editorial Charter

results.title: Communal Kanpur: From the Riots of 1931 to the Violence of 1992.
results.description: Kanpur has witnessed some of the most disturbing episodes of communal violence in modern Indian history. This historical account by Najmuddin A. Farooqi examines the 1931 riots, the Congress Committee of Inquiry, the violence following the Babri Masjid demolition in 1992, the Govind Nagar killings and the long struggle of victims for justice. It also explores the role of administrative failures, communal polarisation and the importance of accountability and communal harmony. The post Communal Kanpur: From the Riots of 1931 to the Violence of 1992. appeared first on ISMA TIMES.
